clue.text: Steadies one in front of Britney Spears

indicators.note: the front of a name is its opening letter, so only the start of the pop star's name is kept

blocks.note: the initial of the singer's first name
one as the article a
spears and lances are both long pointed weapons

explanation.surface: A person steadies themselves ahead of a Britney Spears show, as if bracing for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Spears looks like the singer's surname, but here it is a plural noun for weapons; one goes after the B, giving B + A + LANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: To balance something is to hold it steady, so balances is a verb synonym of steadies.

clue.text: First-class Australian century against English

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for Australian
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
E abbreviates English

explanation.surface: A top-class Australian batsman scores a hundred against England in a cricket Test.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of an Aussie century against England is all abbreviations; against just places one piece beside the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace is an informal adjective meaning excellent or top-rate, the same as first-class.

clue.text: On both sides of gate, notice a gnome

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its outermost letters, so only the ends of gate are kept

blocks.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
taken as written
the first and last letters of gate

explanation.surface: A notice is fixed either side of a garden gate, warning about a garden gnome.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the notice and a above the ends of gate. Gnome is not the garden ornament but an old word for a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome, in its literary sense, is a short maxim or aphorism, which is what an adage is.

clue.text: Fed up? I'm smiling on camera to get lift

blocks.note: the word people say to make themselves smile for a photograph
to doff a hat is to lift it in greeting

explanation.surface: Someone fed up forces a grin for the camera to cheer themselves up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm smiling on camera' stands for what you say when posing: the word photographers ask you to say. Lift is the hat gesture, not cheering up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for annoyed or bored, exactly the mood of being fed up.

clue.text: Area with dry rot rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, something rising is read from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: sec is the wine term for dry
taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: A region of a house afflicted by dry rot that keeps spreading upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry rot reads as one fungal problem, but dry is a separate piece: the French wine label meaning not sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or zone of something, so it serves as a synonym for an area.

clue.text: Tory and scoundrel agree

blocks.note: Con abbreviates Conservative, the party of the Tories
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician and a rogue find themselves in agreement, a cynical political jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share the same opinion, a formal synonym of agree.

clue.text: Dressed as college boy

blocks.note: C is a standard abbreviation for college
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone dressed up as a schoolboy or student, as for a fancy-dress party.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is the old past participle of clothe, meaning clothed or dressed.

clue.text: Enter it if up the spout? Is she now a mummy?

indicators.note: up the spout means ruined or broken, so the preceding letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A smutty question about whether a woman who got pregnant is now a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Up the spout is British slang for pregnant, which makes 'mummy' read as mother; the definition wants an embalmed Egyptian royal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an Egyptian queen of the 14th century BC, so if preserved she would be an embalmed corpse.

clue.text: Uncomfortable one unlacing bustles

indicators.note: to bustle is to move about busily, so the letters are rushed around into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman loosening her corset finds herself ill at ease in the old-fashioned bustle dress.
explanation.walkthrough: A bustle is also a padded frame worn under a skirt, which pairs with unlacing, but here it is a verb shaking the letters up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncongenial is unpleasant or unsuited to one, so it leaves a person feeling uncomfortable.

clue.text: Get to go on live act

indicators.note: one piece is to go on, meaning be placed after, the other in an across clue

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
to get something is to have it

explanation.surface: A performer is told to get on stage and do the live act.
explanation.walkthrough: The stage picture hides a placement instruction: the word for get follows the word for live.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to act or conduct oneself in a particular way, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Large female wearing short coat, one exposed seam that's cut

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter of the garment is dropped
whoever is wearing a garment is inside it, so these letters go within the coat

blocks.note: taken as written before it is trimmed
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
F abbreviates female
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A big woman in a cropped coat shows a seam that has been cut, like a tailoring mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: Seam and cut suggest dressmaking, but they belong to mining: a seam is a layer of coal and the miners cut it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalface is the exposed surface of a coal seam where miners work to extract it.

clue.text: Meeting with former pupil first thing

indicators.note: first places this piece at the front of the answer rather than where the clue mentions it

blocks.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a session is a sitting or meeting

explanation.surface: An early-morning appointment with an old student, first thing in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: First thing reads as a time of day, but first is the placement instruction and thing alone is the definition, as in having a thing about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about someone is an idiom for being preoccupied with them, a fixation.

clue.text: One reduces friction in party with relation

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance party
bearing means relevance or relation, as in has a bearing on

explanation.surface: A diplomatic guest smooths over tensions at a party with a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Friction and relation suggest family quarrels; the definition is mechanical and relation means connection, not kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball bearing is a small steel sphere used in machinery so parts roll rather than rub against each other.

clue.text: Writing solution at side of book by right margin

blocks.note: B abbreviates book
R abbreviates right
ink is the liquid used for writing

explanation.surface: A reader pens a crossword answer in the margin of a book, beside the right-hand edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing solution sounds like filling in an answer, but solution is a liquid here.
explanation.definitionFit: The brink is the very edge of something, so it is a synonym of margin in the sense of border.

clue.text: Go through old coins biting Queen on one

indicators.note: something biting takes another thing between its jaws, so these letters close round the next ones

blocks.note: ex- means former or old
pence are British coins
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone works through a pile of old coins showing the Queen's head, examining each one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, Queen on one stacks the royal cipher above the numeral, and the coins take the pair in just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to undergo or live through it, which is to go through it.

clue.text: Congress controlled by this? Offer to cut fossil fuel withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the fuel's letters run backwards
to cut into a word is to sit inside it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: oil is a fossil fuel
a bid is an offer, as at auction

explanation.surface: A political question: is Congress swayed by bids to slash oil subsidies?
explanation.walkthrough: Congress suggests the US legislature; the definition uses its other sense, sexual intercourse, which is driven by sex drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, the urge that governs whether sexual congress happens; the question mark flags the cryptic definition.

clue.text: Show Dirty Harry is half-hearted

indicators.note: losing half its heart means one of the two middle letters is removed

blocks.note: blue means smutty or obscene
to harry someone is to pester them

explanation.surface: A film review: the Dirty Harry movie is listless and lacking spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirty Harry looks like the Clint Eastwood film, but the words split. Blue Peter is a long-running BBC children's TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Peter is a British television show for children, so show is its category.

clue.text: Turn on old lover with call

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to cite is to summon or call someone, as before a court

explanation.surface: A former partner phones and rekindles the attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone on is to arouse them, and excite is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Lies from Tories — fellows ousting European
Good record label backing trendy star group

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for trendy is read from right to left

blocks.note: G abbreviates good
EMI is a famous record company
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A good record company supports a fashionable group of pop stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Star group invites a band of celebrities; it means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is a constellation, which is a group of stars.

clue.text: Cut musical act

blocks.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance number dropped from a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut looks like a verb about editing the show; it is a noun for a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a hairstyle, and a cut is an informal word for a haircut or style.

clue.text: Complains: parking clamps ultimately put on wheels

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word before it is kept
put on means placed after in an across clue, so these letters follow the vehicle

blocks.note: wheels is slang for a car
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the last letter of clamps

explanation.surface: A motorist grumbles that parking clamps eventually get fixed onto the car's wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: Wheels is slang for a vehicle; the clamping picture suggests a word for grumbling, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble pettily, so carps means complains.

clue.text: Justification to restrict beer

blocks.note: to ration is to limit supply
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone wants a reason to limit drinking at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or grounds behind something, a synonym of justification.

clue.text: Drinks from top of bottles

blocks.note: first meaning: to neck is slang for gulping a drink down
second meaning: the narrow upper parts of bottles

explanation.surface: Someone takes drinks straight from the bottle tops.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of swigging; the two halves are separate meanings, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck is British slang for downing a drink quickly, and also names the slim part near the mouth of a bottle.

clue.text: Food not hot on cold plate

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for the next word from the dish

blocks.note: a dish is a prepared food
H abbreviates hot, as on taps
C abbreviates cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Food served cold rather than hot, laid out on a cold plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen scene hides the tap abbreviations; plate is a flat round object, not crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a flat circular object, and plate can mean a thin flat sheet or round piece.

clue.text: More obscene husband and I parting through strain

indicators.note: parting means splitting open, so these letters push in and divide the next word

blocks.note: to strain a liquid is to filter it
H abbreviates husband
I taken as written, joined to the husband

explanation.surface: A couple split up under the strain of increasingly crude behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Parting and strain suggest a marriage breaking down; strain is a verb for sieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy can mean obscene or smutty, so its comparative filthier means more obscene.

clue.text: One might make a bust by exposing underwear

indicators.note: exposing something strips its covering, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: knickers are women's underpants

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of underwear being bared and a bust on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust and underwear suggest lingerie; a bust is a police arrest, and to nick is British slang for arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who nicks a suspect arrests them, so a nicker is one who makes a bust in police slang.

clue.text: I work out after tablet

indicators.note: after places this piece below the other in a down clue

blocks.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
to go is to work out or succeed, as in make it go

explanation.surface: Someone exercises at the gym after taking a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: I looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: the self.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I, and in psychology it names the conscious self.

clue.text: Adult right to feed metres from magic mushroom?

indicators.note: taking one thing from another removes it, so the unit letter leaves the word
to feed something is to put food into it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written before a letter leaves
m is the symbol for metres
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: Is it right to feed an adult magic mushrooms?
explanation.walkthrough: Magic mushroom reads as one phrase, but magic is fodder and mushroom alone is the definition; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An agaric is a gilled fungus of the kind including the fly agaric, the classic toadstool mushroom.

clue.text: Recovered from vaccination? Went too far

blocks.note: to be over an illness is to have recovered from it
a shot is an injection or jab

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they have got over a jab and admits they overdid it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to go past a target, so overshot means passed the intended point.
